title: I Bow Down, And Fall
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: This shabad opens with i bow down, and fall to the ground in humble adoration, countless times. It turns the heart toward please protect me, and save me from wandering, God. Reach out and give Nanak Your Hand.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels performing, transactional, and dry because the shabad keeps seva inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: Please protect me, and save me from wandering, God. Reach out and give Nanak Your Hand.

lines.gurmukhi: ਡੰਡਉਤਿ ਬੰਦਨ ਅਨਿਕ ਬਾਰ ਸਰਬ ਕਲਾ ਸਮਰਥ ॥
lines.transliteration: dda(n)ddaut ba(n)dhan anik baar sarab kalaa samarath ||
lines.translation: I bow down, and fall to the ground in humble adoration, countless times, to the All-powerful Lord, who possesses all powers.

lines.gurmukhi: ਡੋਲਨ ਤੇ ਰਾਖਹੁ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇ ਕਰਿ ਹਥ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: ddolan te raakhahu prabhoo naanak dhe kar hath ||1||
lines.translation: Please protect me, and save me from wandering, God. Reach out and give Nanak Your Hand. ||1||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: i bow down, and fall to the ground in humble adoration, countless times.
The middle movement widens the correction through please protect me, and save me from wandering, God. Reach out and give Nanak Your Hand.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: please protect me, and save me from wandering, God. Reach out and give Nanak Your Hand.
